title: Seedance 3.0 Spec Rumors
summary: Rumors of a next-generation video model in private development promise long-form generation, multilingual dubbing with emotional expression, directing tools, and lower costs, with implications for the industry.
content:
My last post was a review of Seedance 2.0, and rumors of 3.0 arrived before even a few days had passed. It gives me chills, but it also makes sense. Personally, I think system-level support for LoRAs will be even more powerful than long-form directing (which is already possible by stitching images together). And at one-eighth the price of 2.0, which already costs less than half as much as competing models. Once it launches, won't all those wrappers that help generate long-form videos with consistent LoRAs have to shut down?

-

(The following was automatically translated by X)

Seedance 3.0 has entered its final private development sprint and has achieved several groundbreaking technical leaps!

This generation is no longer content with 15-second short films. It is bringing AI video production into the "feature film era," allowing anyone to create more than 10 minutes of commercial content with a complete storyline, varied camera transitions, and native multichannel dubbing, all from a single sentence!
According to key people involved in the project, Seedance 3.0's main features are as follows.

1. Unlimited continuous generation: Breaking through the length limits of existing models, it can generate seamless videos of 10 minutes or more in a single session (internal tests showed playback of up to 18 minutes without major issues). With its new "narrative memory chain" architecture, the AI remembers earlier plot points, characters' personalities, and scene settings, automatically planning multi-scene sequences, building tension, and devising climactic twists to "tell a story" just like a real director!

2. Native-level multilingual support and emotionally synchronized dubbing: Instead of dubbing in post-production, it uses an end-to-end collaborative learning approach that simultaneously produces dialogue in Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, and other languages, synced to natural lip movements during video generation. It can automatically adjust tone of voice, breathing, crying, and even laughter to match a character's emotions. In test footage, AI-generated dialogue for a martial arts film character delivered results comparable to professional voice acting!

3. Precision directing tools for cinema: Supports "storyboard input" and "real-time directing commands." Users can directly enter instructions such as "Shot 1: wide-angle tracking, the protagonist emerges from the ruins; Shot 2: quick cuts of a car chase with a bass drum beat," and the AI immediately understands and executes them. Built-in industry-standard color presets (IMAX, cinematic style, Netflix color grading, etc.) also allow one-click output and submission for review!

4. Nuclear-grade performance at an ultra-low price: Thanks to next-generation distillation and efficient inference optimization, the computing cost of producing one minute of cinematic video has fallen to one-eighth that of Seedance 2.0. This is a tiny fraction of the cost of producing a single scene through traditional filmmaking. Independent directors, short-form drama studios, and advertisers will experience these remarkable cost savings!
